editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 4, verses 11.4.1–11.4.23; the source prints no Śrīdhara commentary at 11.4.23.

entries.sanskrit: चतुर्थे त्व् अवतारेहा प्रश्नस्योत्तरम् उक्तवान् । जयन्ती-नन्दनो नाम्ना द्रुमिलो नव-सप्तमः ॥ मूर्त्याभिमतयात्मानः [भा।पु। ११.३.४८] इत्य् अनेनात्मनः प्रियम् अवतारं पूजयेद् इत्य् उक्तेऽवतार-ज्ञानम् अपेक्षितं तथा स्तवैः स्तुत्वा नमेद् धरिं [भा।पु। ११.३.५३] इत्य् उक्ते गुण-कर्म-ज्ञानं चापेक्षितम् अतः पृच्छति---यानि यानीति । कर्ता करिष्यति ॥१॥
word_for_word: the answer to the question about the Lord's incarnational activities
entries.literal_english: In the fourth chapter Drumila, the son of Jayantī, answers the question about the Lord's incarnational activities. The earlier instruction to worship a chosen form requires knowledge of incarnations, and the instruction to praise Hari requires knowledge of His qualities and deeds; therefore the king asks which acts the Lord has performed, performs, or will perform.

entries.sanskrit: त्वया पृष्टानि काल-त्रय-संबन्धि-सकलावतार-गुण-कर्माणि कथयितुम् अशक्यानि । सङ्क्षेपतस् तु कानिचित् कथयिष्यामीत्य् आह---यो वा इत्य्-आदिना । अनुक्रमिष्यन् गणयितुम् इच्छति यः स तु बालानाम् इव बुद्धिर् यस्य स मन्द-मतिः । कालेन महता कोऽपि महा-मतिः रजांसि गणयेद् अपि । अखिल-शक्ति-धाम्नः सर्व-शक्त्य्-आश्रयस्य भगवतो गुणांस् तु नैव गणयेत् । तथा च श्रुतिः---विष्णोर् नु कं वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यः पार्थिवानि विममे रजांसि [ऋग्-वेद १.१५४.२४] इत्य्-आदि ॥२॥
word_for_word: all incarnational qualities and deeds connected with the three times
one might count the particles of dust
of the abode of all powers
entries.literal_english: The qualities and deeds of all incarnations across past, present, and future cannot be fully described, though some will be given briefly. A person who tries to enumerate them has childish understanding: even a great intellect might eventually count the earth's dust, but no one can count the qualities of the Lord, the abode of every power.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रादौ पुरुषावतारम् आह---भूतैर् इति । यदा स्व-सृष्टैर् भूतैर् विराजं ब्रह्माण्डं पुरं निर्माय तस्मिन् लीलया प्रविष्टो, न तु भोक्तृत्वेन । प्रभूत-पुण्यस्य जीवस्य तत्र भोक्तृत्वात् ॥३॥
word_for_word: the jīva of abundant merit is the enjoyer
entries.literal_english: The first incarnation described is the Puruṣa. After creating the Virāj universe, conceived as the cosmic city or body, He entered it playfully rather than as its enjoyer; enjoyment belongs to the living being who has accumulated abundant merit.

entries.sanskrit: अस्य गुण-कर्माण्य् आह द्वयेन---यत्-काय इति । यस्य अधिष्ठेयः काय एषः । काय इति सप्तमी वा । तनु-भृतां समष्टि-व्यष्टि-जीवानां ज्ञान-कर्मेन्द्रियाणि यस्य स्वतः स्वरूप-भूतात् सत्त्वात् तनु-भृतां ज्ञानम्, यस्य स्वतः-सिद्धं ज्ञानम् इति वा । यस्य श्वसनतः प्राणाद् बलं देह-शक्तिः, ओज इन्द्रिय-शक्तिः । ईहा क्रिया । याश् च सत्त्वादिभिर् विश्वस्य स्थिति-लयोद्भवे आदि-कर्ता ॥४॥
word_for_word: the body in which He is the presiding support
of collective and individual living beings
knowledge from His own essential being
ojas, the power of the senses
the first agent in creation, maintenance, and dissolution through the guṇas
entries.literal_english: The cosmic body is His support and contains the collective and individual beings. The knowledge and action senses of embodied beings arise from Him; His consciousness supplies knowledge, His prāṇa supplies bodily strength, ojas supplies sensory power, and His activity operates through the guṇas as the first cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

entries.sanskrit: आदि-कर्तेत्य् अनेन तत्-पूर्वकं कर्त्र्-अन्तरम् अपि सूचितम् । तद् दर्शयितुं गुणावतार-द्वारा चराचर-सृष्ट्य्-आदि-कर्तृत्वम् आह---आदाव् इति । यस्येत्य् अनुषङ्गः । यस्य रजसास्य जगतः सर्गे कार्ये शत-धृतिर् ब्रह्मा अभूत् । स्थितौ च विष्णुर् यस्य सत्त्वेनेति शेषः। क्रतु-पतिस् तत्-फल-दाता । द्विजातीनां तद्-धर्माणां च सेतुः पालक इत्य् अर्थः । यस्य तमसा अस्य अप्ययायरुद्रोऽभूत् । इत्य् एतैर् ब्रह्मादिभिर् निमित्त-भूतैः प्रजासुउद्भवादयो यतो भवन्ति स आद्यः पुरुष इत्य् अन्वयः ॥५॥
word_for_word: through the incarnations associated with the guṇas
lord of sacrifice and giver of its fruit
protector of the twice-born and their duties
entries.literal_english: The primordial Person performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution through the guṇa-avatāras: Brahmā in rajas, Viṣṇu in sattva, and Rudra in tamas. Viṣṇu is the lord who gives the fruit of sacrifice and protects the twice-born and their dharma; Brahmā and Rudra serve as instrumental causes of the respective processes.

entries.sanskrit: नर-नारायणावतारम् आह---धर्मस्येति । धर्मस्य भार्यायां दक्ष-दुहितरि मूर्ति-संज्ञायां नारायणो नर इति मूर्ति-द्वयेनाजनिष्ट जातः । तच् चरितम् आह---नैष्कर्म्यम् आत्म-स्वरूपं लक्ष्यते येन तत् कर्म कर्म-निर्हार-रूपं वा उवाच नारदादिभ्यः स्वयं चचार च । योऽद्यापि कर्माचरन्न् आस्ते । ऋषि-वर्यैर् निषेविताव् अङ्घ्री यस्य सः ॥६॥
word_for_word: in Mūrti, the wife of Dharma
the Self whose characteristic is freedom from action
in the form of removing binding action
He spoke to Nārada and the others
whose feet are served by the greatest sages
entries.literal_english: Nara-Nārāyaṇa, the foremost and perfectly peaceful sage, was born from Dharma and Mūrti. He taught Nārada and the other sages the knowledge of naiṣkarmya, the Self's freedom from binding action, and practiced it Himself. His feet are still served by excellent sages.

entries.sanskrit: भगवद्-अवतारत्व-द्योतकं परमोपशमं दर्शयितुम् इतिहासम् आह---इन्द्र इति दशभिः । धाम स्थानं तपसा ग्रहीतुम् इच्छतीति विशङ्क्य तपो-नाशाय कामं स-परिवारं प्रेषयाम् आस । स कामो बदरीभिर् उपाख्यायते । यस् तं तस्याश्रमम् अप्सरो-गणादिभिः सह गत्वा स्त्रीणां प्रेक्षणान्य् एव इषवो बाणाः, तैः। न तस्य महि महिमानं जानातीत्य् अतन्-महि-ज्ञः ॥७॥
word_for_word: supreme tranquility showing the divine incarnation
he wants to seize my position
with spring and very gentle breezes
with arrows that were women's glances
entries.literal_english: The Lord's supreme tranquility reveals His status as an incarnation. Indra, fearing that Nara-Nārāyaṇa wanted his heavenly position, sent Cupid and his company to Badarī. Spring breezes and the side-glances of the women served as Cupid's arrows, because he did not understand the Lord's greatness.

entries.sanskrit: अक्रमम् अपराधम् । अहो ! अहं धीर इति विस्मयो गर्वस् तद्-रहितः । एजमानान् शाप-भिया कम्पमानान् । भो विभो समर्थ ! देव-वध्वः मा भैष्ट । बलिम् आतिथ्यं तान् प्रार्थयते । इमम् अस्माकम् आश्रमम् । आतिथ्याभावे शून्य-प्रायः स्याद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥८॥
word_for_word: the primordial Lord spoke while laughing
O Madana, wind, and wives of the gods
entries.literal_english: Recognizing Indra's improper offense, the primordial Lord laughed without pride and addressed the trembling visitors: “Do not fear, Madana, wind, and wives of the gods. Accept our hospitality and make this hermitage worthy and non-empty by your presence.”

entries.sanskrit: हे नर-देव ! अभय-दे श्री-नारायणे इत्थं ब्रुवति सति, देवाः कामादयः स-व्रीडानि नम्राणि शिरांसि येषां ते । लज्जा-भरेणैवावनत-शिरस्का इत्य् अर्थः । स-घृणं यथा भवति, तथा कृपां जनयन्त इत्य् अर्थः । कृपा-युक्तं तम् इति वा मायातः परे अतोऽविकृते स्वारामाश् च ते धीराश् च ते । तेषां निकरैर् आनतं पाद-पद्मं यस्य तस्मिन् । त्वय्य् एतद् अक्षोभानुकम्पादि न विचित्रम् ॥९॥
word_for_word: those who delight in the Self
whose lotus feet are bowed to by hosts
entries.literal_english: When Nārāyaṇa, the giver of fearlessness, spoke, the gods bowed their heads in shame and addressed Him compassionately. His freedom from change is no surprise: He is beyond māyā, self-delighting and tranquil, and hosts of such sages bow at His lotus feet.

entries.sanskrit: अस्माकं चापराधाचरणं स्वभावत्वान् न चित्रम् इत्य् आहुः---त्वाम् इति । त्वां सेवतां सेवमानानां सुरैर् इन्द्रादिभिः कृता अन्तराया विघ्ना भवन्ति । कस्मात् ? इत्य् अत आहुः---स्वौक इति । स्व-स्थानं स्वर्गम् अतिक्रम्य परमं तव स्थानं व्रजताम् । नान्यस्य त्वाम् असेवमानस्य । कुतः ? बर्हिषि यज्ञे स्व-भागान् पुरोडाशादीन् बलीन् करान् कृषिक इव राज्ञे इन्द्रादिभ्यो ददतः प्रयच्छतः । तर्हि किं मद्-भक्तो विघ्नैर् भ्रश्यति? नेत्य् आहुः---धत्ते इति । यदि इति निश्चये । यतस् त्वं सर्व-सुराधीश्वरोऽविता रक्षकोऽतोऽसौ विघ्नानां मूर्ध्नि पदम् अङ्घ्रिं धत्ते । कुतः पुनस् त्वयि विघ्न-शङ्का? इति भावः॥१०॥
word_for_word: offering the gods their assigned shares in sacrifice
places his foot on the head of the obstacle
entries.literal_english: The gods acknowledge that they place many obstacles before those who serve Nārāyaṇa and try to pass beyond the heavenly abode to His supreme realm. Those who offer each god his sacrificial share do not face such obstacles. But because Nārāyaṇa protects His devotee, that devotee steps on the head of every obstacle.

entries.sanskrit: त्वद्-अभक्तानां तु केवलं तपश्-चरतां द्वयी गतिः । अस्माकं वा वशं यान्ति क्रोधस्य वा । तत्रास्मद्-वशाः कामोपभोगम् अपि तावद् अनुभवन्ति । क्रोधस्य वशाः पुनर् अतिमन्दा इत्य् आहुः---क्षुत्-तृड् इति । क्षुच् च तृट् च त्रि-काल-गुणाच् च शीतोष्ण-वर्षाणि च मारुतश् च प्राणो बाह्यो वा, जैह्व्या जिह्वा-भोगाश् च, शैश्न्या गुह्योपभोगाश् च, एतान् अस्मान् अपार-जलधि-रूपान् अतितीर्य विलङ्घ्य गोष्पदे मज्जन्ति । कुतः ? यतः क्रोधस्य विफलस्य वशं यान्ति गच्छन्ति । किं च, जले मज्जन्तो यथा विवशाः सन्तो मस्तकारोपितं भारम् उत्सृजन्ति, तथा वृथैव न मोक्षाय न च भोगाय शापादिना दुश्चरं तप उत्सृजन्ति ॥११॥
word_for_word: hunger, thirst, the three seasons, and wind
the urges of tongue and genitals
they drown in a cow's hoofprint
entries.literal_english: Those who practice austerity without devotion have two outcomes: they come under the control of desire and enjoy its objects, or they fall under anger. Even after crossing the vast ocean of hunger, thirst, seasons, wind, and the urges of tongue and sex, they drown in a cow's hoofprint when anger conquers them, wasting their hard austerity.

entries.sanskrit: स्त्रियो योग-निर्मिताः स्त्रीः शुश्रूषां कुर्वतीः स्व्-अर्चिताः सुष्ठ्व्-अलङ्कृतास् तेषां स्व-लावण्यादि-दर्पोपशमाय दर्शयाम् आस ॥१२॥
word_for_word: to subdue pride in their own beauty
entries.literal_english: While the visitors praised Him, the Lord displayed women of extraordinary beauty created by yogic power, richly adorned and serving Him. Their purpose was to subdue the visitors' pride in their own beauty.

entries.sanskrit: रूपिणी मूर्ति-मती श्रीर् इव ताः स्त्रियः स्त्रीर् दृष्ट्वा । तासां तु रूपस्यौदार्येण महत्त्वेन हता श्रीः कान्तिर् येषां ते ॥१३॥
word_for_word: their own splendor defeated by superior beauty
entries.literal_english: The attendants of the gods saw women whose embodied beauty resembled Śrī. They were bewildered by the fragrance and their own splendor was diminished by the women's greater beauty.

entries.sanskrit: वृङ्ध्वं वृणीध्वम् । क्व वयं वराकाः ? क्व चेमाः ? इति चेत् तत्राह---स-वर्णां समान-रूपाम् । नैकाप्य् अस्मद् अनुरूपेति चेत्, मा भवतु । तथापि स्वर्गस्य भूषण-रूपाम् ॥१४॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord of the gods, smiling at those who bowed before Him, told them to choose one of the women who was suitable for them, one matching them and destined to become an ornament of heaven.

entries.sanskrit: सुर-वन्दिनो देव-भृत्याः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: receiving the command with the syllable Om
the servants and panegyrists of the gods
placing Urvaśī, the foremost Apsarā, first
entries.literal_english: After receiving the command and bowing, the servants of the gods selected Urvaśī, the foremost of the Apsarās, placed her at their head, and returned to heaven.

entries.sanskrit: इन्द्राय इन्द्रं प्रति नारायण-बलं ऊचुः । शक्रस् तत्रास त्रासं प्राप्तो विस्मितश् च । तत्र विस्मित आसेति वा ॥१६॥
word_for_word: while the residents of the three heavens listened
entries.literal_english: They bowed to Indra in the heavenly assembly and, while all the residents of the three heavens listened, described Nārāyaṇa's power. Indra was both frightened by his offense and astonished by that power.

entries.sanskrit: अन्यान् अप्य् अवतारांस् तच् चरितानि चाह---हंस-स्वरूपीति । दत्तो दत्तात्रेयः । कुमारः सनकादिः । नः पिता ऋषभश् च । विष्णुर् एव कलयावतीर्णः सन्न् आत्म-योगम् अवदत्। तेन विष्णुना हयास्ये हयग्रीवावतारे मधु-भिदा सता ततः श्रुतय आहृताः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: taught the discipline of the Self
Viṣṇu descended in a partial form
the Vedas were brought back in the Hayagrīva form
entries.literal_english: The Lord's other beneficial incarnations include Haṃsa, who taught the discipline of the Self; Dattātreya; the Kumāra; and Ṛṣabha, called the speaker's father. As Hayagrīva, Viṣṇu killed Madhu and recovered the Vedas.

entries.sanskrit: इला पृथ्वी । ओषधयश् च गुप्ताः । क्रौडे च वाराहावतारे । ग्राहाद् गजेन्द्रम् अमुञ्चन् मोचयामास । एवम् आदौ यत्रावतार-नाम नास्ति, तत्र विष्णुः शिवाय जगतां कलयावतीर्ण इत्य् अनुवर्तनीयम् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: in the Fish incarnation Manu, the earth, and the herbs were protected
in the Boar incarnation the son of Diti was killed
the earth was lifted from the waters
in the Tortoise incarnation the mountain was held
He freed the elephant king from the crocodile
entries.literal_english: In the Fish incarnation the Lord protected Manu, the earth, and the herbs through the waters of dissolution. In the Boar form He killed the son of Diti while lifting the earth from the waters; in the Tortoise form He held up the mountain for the churning of nectar; and as Hari He freed the distressed elephant king from the crocodile.

entries.sanskrit: संस्तुन्वतः स्तुतिं कुर्वाणान् ऋषीन् वालखिल्यान् कश्यापार्थं समिधाहरणे गोष्पदे निमग्नान् इन्द्रेणोपहसितान् उद्धृत्यापदोऽमोचयत् । तमसि ब्रह्म-हत्यायां प्रविष्टं मोचयाम् आस । असुर-गृहे पिहिता निरुद्धा या देव-स्त्रियस् ताश् चामुञ्चद् अनेकावतारैः ॥१९॥
word_for_word: submerged in a cow's hoofprint while fetching fuel
entered into the darkness of brahma-killing
wives of the gods confined in an asura's house
He freed them through many incarnations
in Nṛsiṁha, for the safety of the righteous
entries.literal_english: The Lord rescued the Vālakhilya sages when they were submerged in a hoofprint while fetching fuel and were mocked by Indra. He released Indra from the darkness of the sin of brahma-killing and freed the imprisoned wives of the gods from the asura houses. In Nṛsiṁha form He brought fearlessness to the righteous.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तरेषु सर्व-मन्वन्तरेषु कलाभिर् मूर्तिभिर् भुवनान्य् अदधाद् अपालयत् । इमां क्ष्मां समदाद् ददौ ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: During every Manvantara the Lord assumes partial forms, establishes and protects the worlds, and gives the earth. The verse's Vāmana episode is included in this summary: by the pretext of begging, He took the earth from Bali and returned it to Aditi's sons.

entries.sanskrit: हैहयानां कुलस्य अप्ययाय भार्गव-रूपेऽग्निः । स रामो दाशरथिः सन् स-लङ्कं लङ्कायां स्थितम् । स च जयति । वर्तमान-कालीनोऽवतार इत्य् अर्थः ॥२१॥
word_for_word: for the destruction of the Haihaya dynasty
He is Rāma, son of Daśaratha
an incarnation present at the time
entries.literal_english: In the Bhārgava form the Lord is fire for the destruction of the Haihaya dynasty. He is also Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who conquered Laṅkā and triumphs. The present tense is understood to indicate that this incarnation was living at the time of the dialogue.

entries.sanskrit: भाविनं राम-कृष्णावतारम् आह---भूमेर् इति । बुद्धावतारम् आह---वदैर् इति । अतद् अर्हान् यज्ञान् अर्हान् दैत्यान् विमोहयिष्यति । कल्क्य्-अवतारम् आह---शूद्रान् इति । न्यहनिष्यन् निहनिष्यति ॥२२॥
word_for_word: the future Rāma and Kṛṣṇa incarnations
sacrifices performed by those unqualified for them
He will destroy the śūdra rulers
entries.literal_english: The future incarnations are then mentioned: the Lord will descend among the Yadus to lighten the earth and perform deeds difficult even for the gods. As Buddha He will bewilder those unqualified for sacrifice, and at the end of Kali, as Kalki, He will destroy the low-born rulers.

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेन व्याखातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary
entries.note: The pinned source explicitly prints न कतमेन व्याखातम्; no Śrīdhara gloss is invented.
